inputs.share_count_basis: 1,059.27m shares outstanding at 23 Oct 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1.0m dilutive securities (Q3-2026 diluted less basic weighted average). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: LTM to 30 Sep 2026: cash-flow-statement SBC expense 836 (FY2025 829 - 9M-2025 613 + 9M-2026 620) plus tax withholdings on share-based awards 311 (434 - 394 + 271). The two lines are summed because the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation SBC line (LTM 819, incl. payroll tax) is below the cash-flow add-back and so does not absorb the net-settlement taxes.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~0.7 -> cost of equity ~7.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (~4.0% after tax); ~68/32 equity/debt at market -> ~6.6%. Rounded UP to 7.5% as house conservatism for a levered, capital-intensive carrier. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (towers, sites, retail; ~28.7bn of liabilities) is an operating expense inside Adjusted EBITDA, so it is charged in the flows and the operating lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Financing leases (2,294) and tower obligations (3,419, failed sale-leaseback financing) ARE in total_debt, and new financing-lease network equipment (~1.3bn/yr of principal repayments, outside reported capex) is charged forward inside capex_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest. Lumos and Metronet fiber JVs are 50% equity-method investees outside consolidated EBITDA; their carrying value is NOT added in the bridge (loss-making, conservative omission), while the wholesale access fees paid to them are inside EBITDA.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: mature operating company - wireless plus fixed-wireless/fiber broadband). Fresh build, no prior DCF. BASE PERIOD is the last twelve months to 30 Sep 2026, not FY2025: Y1 = Oct-2026..Sep-2027. Using FY2025 as the base would count nine months of 2026 cash flow that has already left as buybacks and dividends and is already reflected in the share count and net debt. LTM revenue 93,816 = FY2025 88,309 - 9M-2025 63,975 + 9M-2026 69,482. reported_fcf is the company's Adjusted Free Cash Flow (OCF 28,717 less PP&E purchases 10,065) and is a LEVERED, post-interest figure (cash interest ~4.1bn); last_fcf follows the house identity (reported - SBC incl. equity taxes - interest income) and is also levered. The projected flows are UNLEVERED (pre-interest) and net debt is deducted at the end, so last_fcf and projected Y1 FCF are not directly comparable: LTM unlevered owner FCF on the forward definition is ~18.5-19bn (OCF 28.7 + interest 4.1 - PP&E 10.1 - spectrum ~1.7 normalised (LTM actual 0.9) - financing-lease principal 1.3 - SBC/equity taxes 1.15). Interest income not stripped: the company is heavily net-debt. total_debt = short-term debt 6,343 + long-term debt 77,323 + tower obligations 3,419 + financing leases 2,294 at 30 Sep 2026. cash and net_debt are adjusted for the 791 of buybacks executed 1-23 Oct 2026 so that they match the 23 Oct share count (balance-sheet cash 5,620). buyback_cash is LTM repurchases (9,974 - 7,528 + 9,564); the flat count is fully funded - the count fell ~5% over the year - plus ~4.4bn/yr of dividends. Price is a regular-session close. Three things reported FCF flatters and the forward build corrects: (1) cash taxes of ~0.8bn LTM against ~4.0bn of book tax (bonus depreciation, deferred tax liability grew 2.1bn in nine months) - cash_tax_rate_path ramps to 24%; (2) spectrum purchases (1.0bn/3.5bn/2.6bn in FY23/24/25) are a recurring capital cost outside 'Adjusted FCF' - charged at ~1.5-1.8% of revenue inside capex; (3) financing-lease equipment. ebitda_margin_path is company Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC) over TOTAL revenue (company quotes it over service revenue: 50%), haircut ~0.5pt for recurring 'Other, net' severance/restructuring and merger-related cash costs that Adjusted EBITDA excludes. No guidance paragraph was available in the extracted filings (guidance is given in earnings releases, not the 10-Q); Y1 is anchored to the Q3-2026 run-rate instead.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic service-revenue growth (~5-6% in 2026 ex-UScellular); equity CAGR unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-2% 5yr, -5% 3yr) because ~44bn of buybacks since 2022 shrank book equity while revenue grew 3.5-5% and EPS compounded 30-68% off a merger-integration trough. Book value is not a usable growth anchor here; EPS and FCF CAGRs are recovery from Sprint integration and are not repeatable.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 annual figures. Owner FCF series = company Adjusted FCF less cash-flow SBC less tax withholdings on share-based awards: FY2022 6,818 (7,656 - 595 - 243; the 7,656 Adjusted FCF includes securitization beneficial-interest proceeds), FY2023 12,622, FY2024 16,114, FY2025 16,732. 5-year FCF CAGR omitted: the FY2020 base is a near-zero merger-integration year. Owner FCF growth has slowed to +3.8% in FY2025; SBC plus equity taxes rose 38% in FY2025 (918 -> 1,263), faster than cash flow.

base.capex_note: PP&E ~10.5% of revenue (LTM 10.7%) + financing-lease equipment ~1.3% + spectrum ~1.8% easing to ~1.5%.
base.wc_note: Negative: equipment-installment and trade receivables, inventory and capitalised contract costs absorb cash as the base grows (FY2025: ~1.3bn of drain beyond interest, tax and merger payments on 6.9bn of revenue growth).
base.da_note: LTM 15.4% includes amortisation of Sprint/UScellular customer intangibles that run off; converges toward the capital-cost run-rate. Spectrum is not book-amortised but is tax-amortisable, so D&A near capex is a fair tax-shield proxy.

scenario_narratives.base: T-Mobile keeps taking share but at a slowing rate. Postpaid account net adds are already down (768k in 9M-2026 vs 919k) and postpaid account churn has risen to 1.09% from 0.97%, so growth leans increasingly on ARPA (155.73, +4% y/y), fixed-wireless and fiber add-ons, and the lapped UScellular base. Revenue growth fades from 5% to 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA margin on total revenue edges from ~40% to 41.5% as UScellular synergies land and scale spreads fixed network cost. PP&E capex holds near 10.5% of revenue with spectrum (~1.5-1.8%) and financing-lease equipment (~1.3%) on top. The cash-tax holiday from bonus depreciation unwinds to a 24% rate by year 7, which holds unlevered owner FCF roughly flat for several years despite EBITDA growth. Terminal value capped at 14x, about today's EV to unlevered owner FCF, so no multiple expansion is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The network lead persists into 5G-Advanced, share gains continue in under-indexed segments (enterprise, smaller markets, top-100 prime accounts), and broadband (8.5m+ fixed-wireless connections, fiber JVs) becomes a second growth leg that lifts ARPA and lowers churn through bundling. Revenue grows 6.5% fading to 3%; margin reaches 43.5% on synergy capture and digital cost take-out; capital intensity drifts down to 12.5% as the 5G build matures and spectrum needs are met from the existing ~100bn portfolio. Needs share gains, pricing power and capex discipline to coincide.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rise in churn is the start of a competitive reset: cable MVNOs keep taking phone net adds, AT&T and Verizon defend with convergence bundles, and T-Mobile's price increases stop sticking. Revenue growth falls to 1.5%, margin erodes from 39% to 37% on promotional and retention spend, and capital intensity stays at 14.2% as fixed-wireless capacity limits force more spectrum purchases and fiber commitments. Cash taxes normalise faster, to 25%. Terminal growth 2% and a 12x cap. Leverage (net debt ~2.3x Adjusted EBITDA) amplifies the equity outcome but there is no solvency issue.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 default to a symmetric 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the leading indicators (postpaid account churn up 12bp y/y, account net adds down 16%) already point the bear's way, and with ~84.5bn of net debt the equity is geared to a margin reset. Base 50%: a slowing but still share-gaining carrier is the central read of the 2026 numbers. Bull cut to 25%: it needs continued share gains, pricing power and falling capital intensity at once in a maturing three-player market facing cable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: T-Mobile is valued on unlevered owner free cash flow built from components, not on the company's Adjusted FCF. Adjusted FCF (~18.7bn LTM, a ~10% yield on the equity) is flattered by a cash-tax holiday, and excludes spectrum purchases, financing-lease equipment and stock compensation; normalising those takes levered owner FCF to roughly 11-12bn. The valuation therefore rests on three judgments: how fast cash taxes normalise, the through-cycle capital intensity including spectrum, and whether the recent rise in churn is noise or the start of a competitive reset. The terminal multiple is capped at today's EV/owner-FCF so the result does not depend on re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash-tax normalisation: each 5pt on the terminal cash tax rate is worth roughly 6-7% of base equity value; the path is a judgment, not guidance.
Competitive intensity: postpaid account churn 1.09% vs 0.97% a year ago and falling account net adds; a 2pt lower terminal margin is the core of the bear case.
Spectrum and fiber capital calls: spectrum purchases are lumpy (1.0-3.5bn/yr) and the fiber JVs carry further funding commitments not modelled in the bridge.
Leverage: ~84.5bn net debt (incl. tower obligations and financing leases) means a 10% change in enterprise value moves equity value ~13-14%.
Terminal value is the capped 14x in base (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would be ~20x); the cap, not the growth rate, sets the terminal value.
Base period is LTM to Sep-2026 and includes UScellular for the full period only from Aug-2025; Y1 growth of 5% assumes ~1pt of residual inorganic contribution early in the year.
Controlling shareholder Deutsche Telekom (majority owner) directs capital allocation; the buyback/dividend programme (up to 18.2bn in 2026) exceeds owner FCF and is partly debt-funded.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 143.75-224.75
data_sources.financials: SEC filings: Form 10-Q for Q3-2026 (balance sheet 30 Sep 2026, cash flow, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, cover-page share count at 23 Oct 2026, post-quarter buybacks), Form 10-K FY2025 (cash flow, spectrum purchases, financing-lease repayments), TMUS_Metrics.csv from SEC XBRL
